findings.finding: The street's bar for the September quarter is adjusted NII $0.34 on revenue $69.38M (Earnings Whispers), while the June quarter printed $0.37 on $69.4M of total investment income; a flat-revenue estimate carrying a $0.03 NII drop looks low unless fees or interest costs jump, so a modest NII beat (about $0.35-0.37) is the likely print. Single estimate source, so capped small.

findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: about two thirds of releases beat and BDC holders treat a small NII beat as the base case. If the market expected a clear beat, the stock would not sit above the July mean target with no move into the print beyond the sector's; it has tracked BIZD.

findings.finding: The December-quarter dividend, which the FY-end release normally discloses, looks set to hold at a $0.30 base: June-quarter NII of $0.37 covered the $0.33 total by 112% and the base by about 123%, and the Fed raised its target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (held on 10-28), a forward lift to floating-rate loan yields that the June-quarter run rate does not yet carry.
findings.why_not_priced: A held dividend is the consensus expectation, so mostly priced; what is not in the run rate is the September hike, which reaches BDC loan coupons with a lag and would show as a firmer NII comment for the December quarter.

findings.finding: OCSL priced $300M of 7.000% notes due 2031 on 2026-09-09 (closed 2026-09-16) to repay revolver debt, ahead of the $350M 2.700% notes maturing 2027-01-15; what the money buys is a refinancing, not a deployment ramp (management called itself defensive and net repayments were -$27.3M in the June quarter), so the fixed coupon on that slice rises by about 4.3 points from January, roughly $0.03-0.04 a share a quarter before any swap effect (whether the 2027 notes were swapped to floating was not found).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no prior OCSL print turned on a refinancing that was found.
findings.why_not_priced: The offering is public, but the NII effect only reaches the run rate from January 2027; if analysts had carried it, the December-quarter consensus would sit visibly below the September quarter's, and no December-quarter estimate was found. It reaches this print through management's FY27 NII and dividend commentary.
